subject: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: security@acmetech.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request

Hi team,

Following up on Acme's SIG review — we've received a request from your security group for a complete list of runtime and telemetry subprocessors that touch customer data for Redwood's hosted and dedicated offerings. To keep things tight for the SIG, could you confirm the scope below is sufficient: 

- All cloud infrastructure providers (compute, storage, networking) used in production
- Telemetry and observability providers (metrics, traces, logging, crashlytics)
- Support and ticketing tools that can access logs or customer identifiers
- Any third parties contracted for patching/OS maintenance or image builds

I've attached a small CSV template (subprocessors_template.csv) — please feel free to use it and return with the vendor name, primary use-case, data types accessed, region(s), and SOC2/HIPAA attestation if available.

Attachments: subprocessors_template.csv, sig_evidence_request.pdf

Next steps: if that scope looks right, we'll fill the template and return by EOD Thursday. If you need additional columns (eg. data flow diagram link), call that out and we'll add it.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: security@acmetech.com
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request

Karthik,

Thanks — scope looks right. Quick clarification: for telemetry we need to know whether logs/metrics are exported outside our tenancy (e.g., to a managed logging backend that centralizes multiple customers). Also please call out any vendors that have cross-region replication of telemetry outside the US.

If you can return the CSV and any current attestation docs (SOC 2 reports or ISO cert links), we'll feed them into our vendor assessment. Preferred turnaround is 3 business days.

Best,
Jae Park
Senior Information Security Analyst
Acme Technology, Inc.
security@acmetech.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:29:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request

Priyom — forwarding Acme's note. Can you pull the current subprocessor roster for hosted, dedicated, and the telemetry pipeline (metric aggregation, logging, traces) and populate the attached template? Key asks from Acme: whether telemetry is replicated outside the US and any attestation links. Also include support tools with log access (PagerOne, Zendesk access, etc.).

I expect a short CSV and links to SOC2 or ISO docs. Target: send back to Jae by EOD Thursday Pacific.

Quoted message below.

— Karthik

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 13:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request

Team — attaching the compiled list (runtime_subprocessors_20261217.csv). Brief summary in the body below.

Attachments: runtime_subprocessors_20261217.csv

Summary (high level):
- Cloud providers: AWS (primary prod: us-west-2), GCP (replica for EU customers), Azure (backup for certain enterprise Dedicated clusters). AWS & GCP have cross-region replication for DR; telemetry may cross regions depending on customer routing config.
- Telemetry: LogStore Inc. (managed logging), TraceWave (tracing), Metricium (metrics). By default telemetry is retained in the customer's region for hosted customers, but for centralized monitoring (some enterprise accounts) we ship metrics to LogStore's US-central endpoints — noted in CSV.
- Support/tools: PagerOne (on-call, limited log access via RBAC), Zendesk (customer support metadata only), NebulaOps (managed OS image builds — access to limited artifacts; no PII), SREOps (internal contractors with restricted access).

Attestations included where available (SOC2 links in CSV). For NebulaOps, we have a pending attestation schedule (vendor says SOC2 in Q1 2027) — I flagged in the CSV and included the contact (j.park@nebulaops.com).

If you'd like, I can redact columns for public-facing copy; otherwise this is the internal roster.

— Priyom
Lead Vendor Compliance Analyst
Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: security@acmetech.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: runtime & telemetry subprocessor declaration request

Hi Jae,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the completed subprocessor roster (runtime_subprocessors_20261217.csv) and links to available attestations. Key notes:

- Telemetry replication: for standard hosted customers, telemetry remains in-region. For accounts using centralized monitoring we flagged the rows and included endpoints; none are replicated outside the US unless the customer explicitly requests EU routing.
- NebulaOps: currently no SOC2; vendor provided expected SOC2 completion Q1 2027 and a contract clause limiting access to build artifacts.
- PagerOne access is strictly RBAC-controlled; scope documented in the CSV.

If you need a redacted version for publication or a data flow diagram, we can produce one next week. Please confirm receipt and any gaps.

Attachments: runtime_subprocessors_20261217.csv

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
